en: Dependent on a state cognizable by some [consciousness], non-visible and non-reacting, there arises a state cognizable by some [consciousness], visible and reacting, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state cognizable by some [consciousness], non-visible and non-reacting, there arises a state not cognizable by any [consciousness], visible and reacting, by way of root condition. Dependent on a state cognizable by some... [and so forth].
Dependent on a state that is cognizable by some, visible, and impinging, there arise states that are cognizable by some,
visible, and impinging, and states that are not cognizable by anyone, invisible, and non-impinging, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not cognizable by anyone, invisible, and non-impinging … [there arise] exactly three.

Dependent on a state that is cognizable by some [consciousness], non-demonstrable, and non-reactive, and [a state] that is not cognizable by any [consciousness], non-demonstrable, and non-reactive … there are three [answers]. (In all cases, nine.

One should formulate nine questions for "cognizable by some, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive" similar to the previous [set]. There are likewise nine questions for "cognizable by some, non-demonstrable, and non-obstructive root.
In the case of root-condition, there are nine; in the case of predominance-condition, nine … pe … in the case of non-disappearance-condition, nine.
